method: Functional threshold power is taken as the power a rider can hold for about an hour. It is either entered directly or derived from one test effort: a 20-minute average multiplied by 0.95, an 8-minute average multiplied by 0.90, or the final minute of a ramp test (maximal aerobic power, MAP) multiplied by 0.75. The product is rounded to the nearest whole watt with halves rounded up, and that integer is used for every zone so the displayed FTP and the bands always agree. The seven Coggan levels are active recovery up to 55% of FTP, endurance 56-75%, tempo 76-90%, lactate threshold 91-105%, VO2 max 106-120%, anaerobic capacity 121-150% and neuromuscular above 150%. Each upper edge is that percentage of FTP rounded to the nearest whole watt; each band then starts one watt above the previous edge, so the zones are contiguous integers and no watt belongs to two zones. Watts per kilogram divides the same watt bounds by the entered body mass and is reported to two decimals; it describes the same power, not a different zone set. The target intensity is a percentage of FTP between 1 and 200, converted to whole watts and labelled with the zone whose watt band contains that power, so the label always matches the number a rider would set on a head unit. FTP and test power are accepted from 40 to 2000 and 2500 watts respectively, body mass from 20 to 300 kilograms, and decimal commas are accepted; blank, non-numeric, exponent-notation and out-of-range values are refused with the failing field named. The test conversion factors are population approximations, not measurements of an individual rider, and watts per kilogram says nothing about aerodynamics, terrain or fatigue. Heart rate, cadence, torque, glycogen use, training-load targets and any medical or performance-diagnostic claim are not modelled.

sources.title: A. Coggan and H. Allen, Training and Racing with a Power Meter: the seven power training levels defined as percentages of functional threshold power.

A. Coggan, training-level guidance for shorter tests: the 0.90 conversion from an 8-minute effort and the ramp-test MAP approximation used at about 0.75.
